headline: Historian discovers 1920s pamphlet revealing RSS and secular activists were actually pen-pals
body:
Q: Professor, you claim to have found a historical document that changes our understanding of ideological tensions. What is it?

A: I found a collection of handwritten postcards in a damp basement in Nagpur. They were written by an early RSS shakha pracharak and a local socialist librarian, exchanging tips on how to grow the perfect marigolds and complaining about the humidity.

Q: Does the correspondence touch upon the complex philosophical debates surrounding unity and religion that leaders discuss today?

A: Hardly. The most heated argument in the entire stack is a three-page rant from 1928 regarding whether or not one should use cow dung manure for roses. The 'ideological divide' seems to have been whether the library should subscribe to more travel magazines or if the shakha members should focus on stationary bicycle training.

Q: How does this reconcile with the modern political discourse where every statement is analyzed for hidden motives?

A: It doesn't. Modern leaders are trying to perform advanced interpretive dance to explain century-old contradictions, while these two men were just trying to figure out if their respective organizations would allow them to collaborate on a local chutney festival without filing a grievance report.
caption: New evidence confirms that before the era of complex political posturing, the biggest ideological struggle in the country was over the correct way to compost. #History #Unity #ChutneyPolitics #NagpurArchives (satire)
igHook: Would you believe that our ancestors were actually just arguing about gardening tips?

sourceHeadline.title: Asaduddin Owaisi says Mohan Bhagwat’s unity remarks at odds with RSS’ views on Muslims

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 7 wins by choosing a grounded, humanizing absurdity (gardening and compost) that bypasses the cynicism of modern political-tech-satire tropes. The specific invented detail of the 1928 argument over cow dung manure for roses provides a vivid, humorous, and affectionate image that distinguishes it from the repetitive 'tech/AI/translator' solutions found in the other candidates.
